_comment: The 88 IAU constellations and their standard three-letter abbreviations.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS: SIMBAD returns Bayer and Flamsteed designations such
as '* alf Ori' and '* 51 Peg'. The trailing token of such a designation is
not a guess about where the star is - it IS the constellation, because the
Bayer/Flamsteed naming system assigns a Greek letter or number WITHIN a
named constellation. Expanding 'Ori' to 'Orion' is therefore a lookup, not
an inference. tools/derive_enrichment.py performs only that lookup and
refuses any designation whose abbreviation is not listed here.
WHAT THIS FILE IS NOT: it is not a constellation BOUNDARY dataset. It
cannot answer 'which constellation contains right ascension X, declination
Y'. Deriving constellation from coordinates needs the IAU boundary table
(Delporte 1930, expressed in B1875 coordinates) plus a B1875 precession
step; UniMap does not carry that dataset and does not approximate it.
See DECISIONS.md D15c.
PROVENANCE CAVEAT: like the attribution strings in tools/sources.json,
this table was transcribed WITHOUT network access and has NOT been checked
against the IAU's published list. The abbreviations are the 1922 IAU
standard and the genitive forms are the conventional ones, but confirm the
table against https://www.iau.org/public/themes/constellations/ before
treating it as authoritative. Only the 32 abbreviations actually present in
the current catalogue are exercised; the rest are carried so a future
import does not silently drop a star.
source: IAU three-letter constellation abbreviations (1922). UNVERIFIED - see _comment.
